research_input.frequency: rank 6 of 42; limits and memory sizing, triggers, SQS to Lambda, function URLs; pairs Lambda vs Fargate vs ECS on EC2 vs EC2 vs Batch; Step Functions vs SQS vs chained Lambdas (chapter 32); RDS Proxy (chapter 26); Lambda@Edge (chapter 15)
research_input.freshness: scaling rate 2023-11; SnapStart Python/.NET 2024-11; streamed 200 MB 2025-07; async 1 MB 2025-10; tenant isolation 2025-11; Managed Instances 2025-11 (90 min 2026-09, not examinable yet); durable functions 2025-12; MicroVMs 2026-06 (not examinable yet); code storage 300 GB 2026-04/07
research_input.note: research input only; every value above is a hypothesis until a saved page quotes it

demand.question: What does Lambda manage for you, and what is left to you (code, configuration)?
What is an event, and what are the two ways an event reaches a function (push by direct invocation, pull by event source mapping)?

Which services push events to Lambda (S3, SNS, EventBridge, API Gateway, ALB, Cognito, Step Functions) and which does Lambda poll through an event source mapping (SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, Kafka, MQ, DocumentDB)?
demand.note: Source lists ESM services: DocumentDB, DynamoDB, Kinesis, MQ, MSK, self-managed Kafka, SQS (lambda-services table, invocation-eventsourcemapping). Kafka, MQ and DocumentDB rows not adopted as separate facts.

demand.question: What is the difference between a synchronous and an asynchronous invocation: who waits, who retries, where the event is queued?
Which services invoke synchronously (API Gateway, ALB, function URL, Cognito, CloudFront) and which asynchronously (S3, SNS, EventBridge, CloudWatch Logs)?
demand.note: Function URL and CloudFront are not rows of the lambda-services table; function URLs are direct invocation (lambda-invocation page).

demand.question: Why must a function be stateless; where should state live (DynamoDB, S3, EFS)?
What are the Init, Invoke and Shutdown phases; what is a cold start; why is a warm environment reused?
How long may initialization code run (the 10-second Init limit; the exceptions for provisioned concurrency, SnapStart and Managed Instances)?
Does the guide say Lambda is best suited for short invocations (one second or less), even though a standard invocation may last 15 minutes?
Is a function spread across several Availability Zones in a Region; are there maintenance windows?

What are the benefits and trade-offs of event-driven design in the guide (replacing polling and webhooks, loose coupling, variable latency), and the listed anti-patterns (monolith, recursive patterns, synchronous waits)?
What does the guide call the two programming models (standard functions up to 15 minutes; durable functions up to one year)?
What is the memory range of a function (128 MB to 10,240 MB) and the increment (1 MB)?
How is CPU allocated (in proportion to memory); at what memory does a function get one vCPU (1,769 MB)?
What are the default (3 seconds) and maximum (900 seconds, 15 minutes) timeout values?

Hypothesis (FRESHNESS, 2026-09-09, after the exam cutoff): on Lambda Managed Instances, asynchronous and event-source-mapping invocations allow a timeout up to 5,400 seconds (90 minutes); synchronous calls keep 15 minutes. Label: not examinable yet.
demand.note: The quotas and timeout pages state 5,400 seconds (90 minutes) for async and event source mapping invocations except Amazon MQ and Amazon DocumentDB. The What's New feed dates Lambda Managed Instances itself 2025-11-30; the 90-minute date (FRESHNESS 2026-09-09) is for the decisions+changes lens to confirm.

demand.question: What is the range of /tmp ephemeral storage (512 MB to 10,240 MB)?
What are the deployment package limits: 50 MB zipped, 250 MB unzipped including layers; larger uploads go through S3?
What is the maximum container image size (10 GB uncompressed)?
How many layers can a function have (5), and do layers work with container-image functions (no)?
What is the environment-variable limit (4 KB in aggregate)?
What are the payload limits: 6 MB synchronous request and response, 1 MB asynchronous, 200 MB streamed response?
What is the Lambda-managed code storage quota per Region (300 GB) and is it increasable (no; self-managed S3 code storage instead)?
demand.note: The developer guide quotas page says 300 GB is 'Not increasable'; the General Reference quotas table (docs/general/latest/gr/lambda-service, row 'Function and layer storage') lists 300 Gigabytes as Adjustable: Yes. The developer guide is taken as current truth.

demand.question: What is the default concurrent-executions quota (1,000 per account per Region) and how far can it be raised (tens of thousands, through Service Quotas)?
What is the per-function concurrency scaling rate (1,000 execution environments every 10 seconds), and does the guide state the old account-wide burst limits anywhere?
demand.note: The old account-wide burst limits (500 to 3,000 per Region) are not stated on any saved guide page. lambda-concurrency page, section 'Understanding concurrency and requests per second', says 'A function using on-demand concurrency can experience a burst increase of 500 concurrency every 10 seconds, or by 5,000 requests per second every 10 seconds, whichever happens first.' The same page's scaling-rate section, scaling-behavior, the quotas page and the General Reference all say 1,000 every 10 seconds. No fact was added for the 500 example.

demand.question: What formula does the guide give for concurrency (requests per second multiplied by average duration in seconds)?
What happens on throttling: a synchronous caller gets a 429 (TooManyRequestsException); an asynchronous event is retried from the internal queue; an event source mapping backs off?
What does reserved concurrency do (a maximum for the function and a guaranteed slice of the account pool, at no charge), and what does reserved concurrency 0 do (stops all invocations)?
Does the account always keep 100 units of unreserved concurrency for functions without reserved concurrency?

What is provisioned concurrency (pre-initialized environments, no cold start), does it require a version or alias (not $LATEST), and can it scale on a schedule or a metric with Application Auto Scaling?

SnapStart versus provisioned concurrency: which runtimes support SnapStart (Java, Python, .NET), is SnapStart best-effort, and when does the FAQ recommend provisioned concurrency (strict double-digit millisecond startup)?
demand.note: Source differs from older material: the guide now says SnapStart supports ZIP and container image deployments (Java 11+, Python 3.12+, .NET 8+). 'Best-effort' wording is in the FAQ fact only.

demand.question: What is the network bandwidth per execution environment (625 Mbps) and the raised ceiling for functions outside a VPC (3,000 Mbps; FRESHNESS 2026-08-05, not examinable yet)?
What is the ENI-per-VPC quota that VPC functions share with EFS (3,000)?
demand.note: The decision guide docs/decision-guides/latest/decision-guides/fargate-or-lambda says 'ENIs are an exhaustible resource with a soft limit of 250 per Region.' The Lambda quotas page and the General Reference say 3,000 elastic network interfaces per VPC. The quotas pages are current truth; no fact was added for 250.

demand.question: Does more memory shorten duration enough that cost stays flat or falls; what does the guide say about choosing memory (Power Tuning, CPU-bound work)?
demand.note: No saved page states that more memory keeps cost flat or lowers it. Looked in configuration-memory, best-practices, www/lambda/pricing (search 'memory', 'cost'). Keep the claim qualitative.

demand.question: Which Lambda API rate limits matter (GetFunction, Invoke) and which quotas are listed in the General Reference page for Lambda?
demand.note: The General Reference lists no separate Invoke API rate; invocation is limited by concurrency (10 requests per second per environment for synchronous calls).

demand.question: Do new AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas that AWS raises automatically?
Well-Architected REL01-BP01: how should a team track quotas for a standby environment (Service Quotas, quota monitoring, requesting increases before failover)?
demand.note: From REL01-BP01 page; REL01-BP06 is only a linked title there (not fetched).

demand.question: Asynchronous retries: how many times does Lambda retry a failed asynchronous invocation by default (two more times), with what waits (one minute, then two minutes)?
What are the asynchronous configuration ranges: maximum event age (60 seconds to 6 hours, default 6 hours) and maximum retry attempts (0 to 2)?
demand.note: The 60-second minimum is stated only in the API reference (Valid Range: Minimum value of 60. Maximum value of 21600.); the developer guide says 'up to 6 hours'. The default of 6 hours is stated as a default only for throttling and system-error retries (lambda-async-throttle-retry-6-hours).

demand.question: What is a dead-letter queue for a function (SQS queue or SNS topic, asynchronous invocations only), and how does it differ from an on-failure destination?
What can a destination target (SQS, SNS, Lambda, EventBridge; S3 for failed events) and does the guide recommend destinations over a dead-letter queue?
demand.note: No saved sentence says 'destinations are recommended over DLQ'; the retain-records page presents a DLQ as an alternative. Not found as a recommendation.

demand.question: Event source mapping basics: batch size, batching window, filter criteria, partial batch responses (ReportBatchItemFailures) and tags.
demand.note: Tags on event source mappings not mined.

demand.question: SQS to Lambda: what are the batch size defaults and maximums (10 by default; up to 10,000 for standard queues with a batching window), and what is the maximum concurrency setting range for an SQS event source (minimum 2)?
SQS to Lambda scaling: how many pollers does Lambda start with and how fast does it add them (initial 5 concurrent batches, up to 300 more per minute, up to 1,000 batches or the account quota)?
demand.note: Expected a ceiling of 1,000 batches; services-sqs-scaling says one event source mapping can process up to 1,250 concurrent invokes (100,000 in provisioned mode). Start of five batches and up to 300 more concurrent invokes per minute match. | register-18: the demand hypothesis (1,000) is contradicted; the guide says 1,250 per event source mapping (100,000 in provisioned mode).

demand.question: SQS to Lambda failure path: a failed batch returns to the queue after the visibility timeout; the queue's redrive policy sends messages to the queue's dead-letter queue; the guide's advice to set the visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout.

Streams (Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams): one concurrent invocation per shard, parallelization factor up to 10, in-order processing, retries until the record expires, bisect batch on error, on-failure destination.
demand.note: 'One concurrent invocation per shard' is not stated in those words; the guide states the parallelization factor default of 1 concurrent batch per shard.

demand.question: Event filtering: can a filter on the event source mapping drop records before the function runs, and does a dropped record cost an invocation?
demand.note: Dropped records are discarded and not sent to the function; no saved Lambda page states whether a dropped record is billed. Looked in invocation-eventfiltering and www/lambda/pricing. Only a What's New feed post says filtering prevents unnecessary invocations (not evidence).

demand.question: Recursive loop detection: which services does Lambda watch (S3, SQS, SNS), and what happens when a loop is detected (the function is stopped after about 16 recursive invocations)?
demand.note: Source adds Amazon EventBridge custom event buses and pure Lambda-to-Lambda loops to S3, SQS, SNS.

demand.question: Idempotency: why can an event be delivered more than once (at-least-once delivery from asynchronous invocation and event source mappings), and what does the guide recommend?

FAQ: how many times is an asynchronous invocation retried (the FAQ says at least 3 times) and how long are Kinesis and DynamoDB stream records kept (at least 24 hours)? Note the wording difference from the guide (two more times).
demand.note: Guide (two more attempts after the first) is current truth; FAQ wording 'at least 3 times' counts all attempts. | register-18: the FAQ fact 'retried at least 3 times' was rejected (contradicts the guide's two retries, configurable 0 to 2).

demand.question: What does S3 do with events that Lambda throttles (the FAQ says S3 may retain and retry for 24 hours) and how long can asynchronous invocations absorb a burst before events are rejected?
demand.note: register-18: the FAQ fact on 15-30 minutes of burst absorption was rejected (older wording; the guide retries throttled events for up to 6 hours).

demand.question: Function URLs: a dedicated HTTPS endpoint per function or alias; auth types AWS_IAM and NONE; CORS; when a function URL is enough and when API Gateway is needed (usage plans, API keys, WAF, caching, request validation).
Application Load Balancer as a trigger: the ALB invokes the function synchronously through a Lambda target group; what limits apply to the response?
demand.note: Response limits for ALB Lambda targets are not on the Lambda services-alb page; they are in the ELB user guide (lambda-functions page, not saved). Pointer to the ELB chapter.

demand.question: API Gateway with Lambda: proxy integration, synchronous invocation, the integration timeout the API imposes (pointer to the API Gateway chapter).
demand.note: The API Gateway integration timeout is not stated on services-apigateway; belongs to the API Gateway chapter.

demand.question: Scheduled invocation: EventBridge Scheduler (cron and rate expressions, flexible time windows, retry policy, dead-letter queue) replaces cron jobs on a server.
demand.note: Dead-letter queue for Scheduler not stated on the Lambda page (stated: retry limits and maximum retention time).

demand.question: Response streaming: which invocation paths support it (function URLs, the Invoke API with the streaming mode), the 200 MB limit and the bandwidth rule (uncapped for the first 6 MB, then 2 MBps).
demand.note: close-facts-18: lambda-streaming-bytes-price rejected at finalize (disputed after repair); the price is not part of this question.

demand.question: Durable functions versus Step Functions: what durable functions add (checkpoint and replay, waits without compute cost, up to one year), and when the guide still recommends Step Functions.
Step Functions with Lambda: the Task state invokes functions; why orchestration beats chaining functions with direct invokes (pointer to chapter 32).

A function attached to a VPC: it gets ENIs in the subnets you choose, has no public IP, and reaches the internet only through a NAT gateway in a private subnet; a public subnet alone gives no internet access.
Which execution-role permissions does a VPC function need (AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole: ec2:CreateNetworkInterface and friends), and which quota does it consume (ENIs)?

Can a VPC function reach AWS services privately through VPC endpoints (gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB, interface endpoints), and can clients inside a VPC invoke Lambda over an interface endpoint?
